title: CancellationToken Fundamentals
summary: Understand cooperative cancellation in .NET and propagate an HTTP caller's cancellation through asynchronous work.
objectives: Explain why cancellation in .NET is cooperative.
Pass CancellationToken through cancellable asynchronous call chains.
Distinguish requested cancellation from unexpected application failure.

sections.heading: A signal, not a force kill

reviewCandidates.prompt: What should a method normally do with the CancellationToken it receives?
reviewCandidates.answer: Pass it to downstream operations that support cancellation, so the caller's request to stop can reach the work actually in progress.

reviewCandidates.prompt: What problem can occur when a request is cancelled but downstream I/O continues?
reviewCandidates.answer: Abandoned work still consumes connections and other resources. Cancellation is cooperative: downstream operations must receive and observe the signal to stop.

reviewCandidates.prompt: Why should requested cancellation not automatically be treated as an unexpected application error?
reviewCandidates.answer: OperationCanceledException can represent the caller intentionally abandoning work, not a server defect. Preserve that outcome instead of swallowing it or reporting false success.
